messages:
alexa: Quick flag — eng-platform wants to change default SDK routing to server-side policy so the platform can do smart fallbacks. Need a SDK compatibility plan. Might be surprising for apps that relied on client-side explicit routing.

mike: Do we have a short spec or is this still fuzzy? :eyes:

alexa: @mike Short: backend will accept missing routing param and apply a server policy. Previously missing meant clients behaved as 'explicit' and stuck to what callers asked. Full spec is in the internal doc (link: https://go/redwood/routing-v2).

sam: That is a semantic break — apps that depend on explicit routing could get different traffic. We need a clear migration path.

lina: Could SDKs expose an opt-in flag first? e.g., client = Redwood(..., routing_mode='server') so it's opt-in, not invisible.

pranav: DevEx: For Python/TS/Go, we need: warning logs, telemetry headers to detect adopters, and a Console deprecation banner. Also a staged rollout plan.

jess: Telemetry is crucial. Proposed headers: `x-rd-client-routing: <explicit|server|legacy>` and `x-rd-client-version`. That lets us count who will break.

alexa: Proposed rollout: 1) SDKs add header telemetry + warn log. 2) Console shows deprecation banner and per-org opt-in toggle. 3) Backend applies server policy by default only for orgs that opt-in; after 60 days flip default for all new requests. 4) Full flip after 6 months. Feedback?

mike: For SDKs we must avoid breaking signatures. Idea: add new param `routing` default None. If None -> send header 'legacy' for now. After flip, None -> 'server'. Also allow explicit 'server' or 'explicit'.

sam: Example patch for Python to illustrate approach:
```python
# before
client = RedwoodClient(api_key)
# after
client = RedwoodClient(api_key, routing=None)  # None => legacy behavior until flip
# to opt-in now
client = RedwoodClient(api_key, routing='server')
```

lina: TS equivalent:
```ts
// before
const c = new Redwood({ apiKey })
// after
const c = new Redwood({ apiKey, routing: undefined }) // sends legacy header
const c2 = new Redwood({ apiKey, routing: 'server' })
```

pranav: I'll implement header ingest on the backend and an org-level metric showing counts per header value. That will be surfaced in Console > Traffic Insights. Also will add an internal debug endpoint to sample affected requests.

jess: UX idea: Console toggle should have a "preview" mode that routes only X% (default 10%) through server policy and shows delta in latency/cost and model choice. That makes it safer for product teams to validate.

alexa: Action items: DevEx SDK changes (py/ts/go) + telemetry backend + console toggle + changelog + migration guide. I'll draft an RFC and checklist. Who owns SDK patches?

mike: I can take TS SDK changes. @lina will you own Python? @pranav can you do Go + backend telemetry?

lina: Yep — I'll add a warn log on first client init when routing=None and include migration notes in the release.

pranav: I'll add header ingestion, per-org metrics, and the debug sampler endpoint. Will coordinate the 10% preview infra with @jess.

jess: I'll prototype the Console toggle UI and the preview experiment wiring to our rollout service. Also will add an analytics panel to show expected cost change.

deploy-bot: Note: design thread — no deploy scheduled.

alexa: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC by EOD with a rough timeline. If anyone spots issues with the plan call them out here. :thumbsup:
